newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares seen bullish over the week.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares seen bullish over the week.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares are expected to stay bullish this week, driven largely by improved liquidity on the equity market, brokers said on Tuesday.
The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange posted another firm and active performance on Tuesday with the key industrial index leaping 74.09 points to close at 10,511.49.
"Liquidity was an obvious driving factor with buyers willing to chase sellers above previous limits," one broker said.

"I'm not sure where the money is coming from, probably from the money market where there could have been some maturities but liquidity seems to be the factor driving the stock market and I don't see why it shouldn't continue to firm (over the week)," he said.

Among Tuesday's winners, merchant banker NMB jumped 150 cents to 3,300 as did departmental stores Haddon and Sly to 450, restaurant and hotel group Meikles rose 100 cents to 3,000 and bankers Barclays gained 50 cents to 3,300.

Non-carbonated crushes and syrups manufacturer Schweppes and tea and coffee producer EHPL added 15 cents each to 360 and 250 respectively while blue-chip supermarkets and beverages conglomerate Delta at 1,765 and transport group Clan at 210 both added 15 cents.
Against the trend, pharmaceutical group Caps dropped 200 cents to 2,800, agricultural companies investor Chemco shed 100 cents to 4,500 and tobacco firm TSL lost 15 cents to 620.

Minings were a bit firmer too with Wankie Colliery adding five cents to 580 in good volumes while brokers said they saw strong buying support in gold producer Falgold despite recent lows in the bullion price.
The mining index put on 1.87 points to 863.90.
